llm-rule-adjudication technique sourced

LLM-adjudicated state transitions (LLM as game mechanic)

A language model computes the outcome of an interaction (two elements combined, an action on an object) from a text description of the inputs, with results cached so every player sees the same rule.

Generative world model2024Shipped (niche)determinism Mitigable5 mechanics affected
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

mechanism

The game describes the inputs (two items, or an object state plus an action) as text and asks the model for the result, constrained to a short name, an icon, or a small state diff. Infinite Craft first looks the pair up in a database; only a never-tried pair goes to the model (Llama 2, later Llama 3.1), and the answer is stored, so the rule becomes fixed and shared by all players after the first query and the first finder is credited. The cache turns a stochastic model into a growing deterministic rule table and bounds cost to unique queries. Benchmarks of LLMs as text world simulators measure how often the predicted next state matches the true one.

limitations

  • Accuracy: as a general state simulator GPT-4 is right on whole-state transitions at most 59.9% of the time, so errors compound over multi-step dynamics.
  • Legibility: generated rules follow word association rather than a learnable system, so players cannot predict outcomes from principles.
  • Cost and load scale with unique queries; Infinite Craft's traffic overloaded its servers.
  • Outputs must be filtered for offensive results because every cached answer becomes permanent shared content.

affects

Collection goals

Collections become open-ended races to discover never-generated items, with a First Discovery credit for the first player to create each one.

Enables new form
affects

Combination discovery

A language model decides the result of each new combination and caches it, turning a finite authored recipe graph into an open one (Infinite Craft).

Enables new form
affects

Generative content on demand

Generated results are written back as shared, persistent rules rather than one-off text, so the world's content grows with play and stays consistent across players.

Deepens
affects

Hand crafting

The recipe space becomes unbounded: any pair of items yields a generated result rather than a lookup in a finite designer table, and the first answer is cached as the permanent recipe.

Enables new form
affects

Material interactions

Interactions between arbitrary materials or elements can be resolved by a model rather than an authored pair table, but whole-state accuracy near 60% means results must be bounded to simple outputs and cached.

claims

3 with sources
c01high

Infinite Craft (January 2024) starts from water, fire, wind, and earth and generates a new element and emoji with Llama 2 and Llama 3.1 for any untried pair, storing the result so each pair gives every player the same answer.

src-wikipedia-infinite-craft

c02high

On 76,369 transitions from 31 text games, GPT-4 predicted the full next state correctly at most 59.9% of the time, up to 77.1% for action-driven and at most 49.7% for environment-driven changes; humans scored about 80% on a subset where GPT-4 scored about 50%.
